stem.en: You shout your own name from a hillside. A second or so later you hear your own name again, coming from the same direction across the valley. There is nobody standing on the rock face.

text.en: Somebody on the far side shouted it back, because the delay was long enough for a person to react and repeat what they heard.
Your own ears repeated the sound on the way in, because a loud shout makes the ear drum vibrate a second time after the sound has already passed.
The same shout travelled to the rock face across the valley and reached your ears again on its way back, so the second voice was your own arriving twice.
A hillside gives back whatever is shouted at it, which is why people shout at rocks in the first place and why nobody shouts at a bedroom wall.

explanation.en: Nothing made the sound a second time. One shout went out in every direction at once, and the piece of it that crossed the valley reached the rock face and came back to your ears a moment later - so what you heard the second time was your own shout, delayed by the journey out and back. The reason the same trick does nothing in a bedroom is not that a wall refuses to return sound; it is that the wall is close enough for the return to arrive before you have registered the first one.

hints.en: Check each option against one fact you are certain of: nobody was there, and you heard it a second or so later.
The voice was unmistakably yours. Which of the four options can explain how your own shout was still in the air when it reached you again?
